messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-p99 > 1200ms for api-prod-us-west on route /v1/generate — triggered at 2024-10-22T21:02:36Z. ping: @ops-oncall. dashboard: https://console.redwood.example/d/latency/realtime?org=prod :rotating_light:

ops-oncall: saw it, joining bridge. paging now. @devin @maya please stand by, collecting quick checks.

devin: joining. first glance — p99 jump is concentrated on streaming endpoints, spike aligns with increased inflight streaming connections on node pool gpu-pool-west-3. KV cache hitrate dropped ~30%.

maya: dashboard snapshot: p95 from 180ms -> 520ms, p99 from 420ms -> 1.3s. streaming queue length +220. errors not trending up (5xx ~ baseline). looks like slow tail / cold-kv behavior.

sri: quick list to run: 1) check node restarts `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-pool-west-3` 2) check AGG queue lengths in tracing UI 3) kvcache stats `GET /internal/kvcache/stats`

devin: ran pod check — 2 pods restarted in last 3m (OOM kill on runtime-worker-7). link: https://k8s.redwood.example/pods/runtime-worker-7

ana: any customer impact? are any customers reporting 5xx or timeouts? @support?

maya: support says no active error pages, but a few large customers flagged elevated response times via their synthetic monitors. no requests dropped, just slow.

infra-lead: probable root candidate: KVCACHE eviction storm after a small rolling restart (OOMs) clearing prefix cache -> high seq length recompute + heavier kernel paths. also GPU queueing cascades latency.

ops-oncall: mitigation proposal: 1) enable temporary route-shift for critical customers to eu-secondary region, 2) enable burst-capacity pool (dedicated spare nodes), 3) avoid large batching for streaming routes (set batch_size=1) — execute in that order. anyone object?

sri: +1 on route-shift and burst. for batching config, we can flip route config with one-line change:```json
PATCH /api/v1/routes/realtime
{ "batching": { "max_tokens": 1, "enabled": false } }
```

devin: I'm prepping a quick rollback-safe playbook: 1) create canary rule for route with `weight: 0.2` to redirect 20% -> eu-secondary, 2) monitor p99 over 1m windows, 3) if p99 drops by >30% promote to 100%.

maya: executed canary redirect 20% -> eu-secondary at 21:06:10Z. observing metrics — p99 on canary popped to 480ms (good), origin still high.

ops-oncall: enabling burst-capacity now (scale up +2 nodes to gpu-pool-west-3).

infra-lead: scaling complete at 21:08:45Z. GPU queue length dropped ~40%. KV cache warming in progress.

devin: after canary and scale, origin p99 down to 750ms and counting down. canary stable at sub-500ms.

ana: customer comms — support drafting note: "we observed elevated latencies on streaming generation earlier; we applied routing and extra capacity; performance is returning to normal. Monitoring ongoing."

ops-oncall: good. we keep bridge for 30m. action items: infra to root-cause OOMs on runtime-worker-7 (OOM threshold tuning), runtime to add safer kvcache warmup + prefills, product to review batching defaults for streaming.

infra-lead: grabbing OOM logs and the node metrics; will file INC-2024-314 and attach findings.

devin: follow-up checklist I pushed to the incident doc: https://docs.redwood.example/incidents/1718923456 — includes commands I ran and a smoke test script.

ops-oncall: thanks team. monitoring 15m window; if p99 stays <600ms and no new restarts, we'll close the active page and follow up with RCA. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident note: page opened at 1718923456, mitigations applied (route-canary, scale-up) at 1718923973, status: monitoring.

ops-oncall: closing live page in 5m if stable. last check 21:14:24Z p99=510ms, p95=240ms.

maya: will keep an eye overnight and hand off to tomorrow's oncall.

ana: moving to postmortem workflow once infra posts logs. thanks all. :clap:
